reason: Under the transfer/leakage lens both the original rule and the refined 'distinct-nucleus fill' fail. (1) The payoff is measured only at ANNOTATED nodes, and that is exactly where the in-sample detector puts sub-threshold mass. Friend A's full-frame 0.90 pass recovers 151/151 GT divisions (136 at 0.965; 44b6 26/26, 6bba 125/125) and adds +24% candidate nodes: on train, weak peaks sit on annotated cells with near-perfect recall. Step-0 coverage, the GO criterion of both variants, is therefore an in-sample number that cannot be checked out of sample. All public weights saw all 199 videos, and no embryo-held-out detector exists (exp11 B was fine-tuned from the public pretrained model, which had seen 44b6). (2) For the original rule this is the classic leak signature. Its fills land on the 4-6 um 'holes' (about 73% of hole nodes), which the image-valley test shows are the SAME blob as our node (no dip in 95-99% of cases). A 0.90 peak there is a secondary mode the detector learned AT THE ANNOTATION POSITION, and annotations sometimes sit on cell corners. Locally it matches GT and looks like a TP. On test the annotation positions are unknown to the model, so the same rule adds a flank duplicate that steals links: the hengck23 failure mode and the forum pattern 'min-track-len +0.013 offline / -0.004 public'. (3) The node-multiplier cost is certain on test: +1.0-1.5% nodes = -0.0009 to -0.0014. The edge gain is not certain. The refined variant's realistic local gain is +0.001 to +0.004 (ceiling about 1,950 FN x 7.5e-6 = +0.015, times 15-30% coverage, times ~0.6 linking success). After a >= 50% in-sample haircut the public expectation is 0 to +0.001, which is inside LB noise and net of a node cost of the same size. (4) The refined variant targets >7 um persistent misses, the same territory as x138 readmit (>= 0.965, within 4 um of an open end) and gapfill (>= 0.5 peaks, <= 3% nodes). Each of those was neutral on LB on its own, and the refined rule is a stricter subset of that territory, so the prior for its LB effect is ~0. The >7 um misses are cells the detector failed to fit even in-sample, so on unseen embryos their sub-threshold peaks will be weaker still. (5) Chains of 3 nodes die at min_track_len 6 unless they attach to an existing track. That makes the gain depend on relink, the most transfer-fragile stage: relink-off won locally and lost 0.002 on LB. (6) 44b6 redundancy: the 44b6 videos are overlapping crops of one recording with 0.2-1.3% label coverage. A persistent miss in an overlap region is counted in several crops, so the per-embryo gate on 44b6 rests on a handful of real events, as the stitch case shows (59/71 videos unchanged).
fix_if_any: Only a leakage-controlled version could survive, and it ranks below the coordinate head and same-blob duplicate merging. (a) Before any replay, run a GT-free leakage diagnostic on the step-0 peak cache. Compute the trigger rate (clearance >= 6.5 um, valley < 0.85, 3-chain) at ANNOTATED distinct blobs and at UNANNOTATED distinct blobs, where a distinct blob is a kept node or a peak whose valley test confirms a separate nucleus. Take the matched-position proxy for unannotated cells from nuclei in the same videos away from GT lineages. If the annotated rate exceeds the unannotated rate by more than 1.3x, the local coverage is leakage and the idea stops. (b) Compute the step-0 gain as if the annotated trigger rate equalled the unannotated one (transfer-corrected coverage), and require the corrected local estimate to be >= +0.003 after the node cost. (c) Require the node ratio to stay <= +0.5%, and require >= 80% of inserted chains to attach to an existing track. Unattached tracklets carry node cost with no scored edges on test. (d) Report 44b6 per leak group, not per crop. (e) The only real transfer test is an embryo-held-out detector (train on 6bba, run on 44b6 and the reverse), which is GPU work and closed as 'detector fine-tunes'. Without it no LB slot should go to this idea before 29 Sep.
realistic_public_gain: Original clearance 4.5 + 6 um sandwich rule: -0.001 to -0.003 (duplicate flank nodes plus a certain node penalty; local gains would come mostly from in-sample secondary modes at annotation positions). Refined distinct-nucleus fill: 0 to +0.001 public, which is not separable from LB noise and is net of a -0.0009 node cost at +1%. Not worth a probe slot against the x138 coordinate head or same-blob duplicate merging.
